speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient with a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain following antibiotic treatment. To understand your condition better, can you tell me which specific antibiotic you were taking and for how many days?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Induced Maculopapular Exanthem (Drug Eruption)

The history of a delayed-onset rash starting in flexural areas (antecubital and popliteal fossae) after one week of amoxicillin therapy is classic for this reaction. While we must rule out viral exanthems like Roseola or Parvovirus B19, the temporal relationship and specific distribution strongly favor a drug-induced etiology. Given your age and the description of generalized joint pain, could you confirm if the joint pain is symmetrical and if the rash has become more pruritic or confluent over the last 48 hours?
